12.name: Mahatma Gandhi
12.significance: Pioneered the philosophy and strategy of nonviolent civil disobedience (Satyagraha) that liberated India from colonial rule and inspired international civil rights and freedom movements worldwide, including those led by Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.

13.name: Swami Vivekananda
13.significance: Introduced the ancient Indian philosophical schools of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world with his historic 1893 address at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago. Revitalized India's cultural confidence and spiritual renaissance, advocating selfless service to humanity.

14.name: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
14.significance: Led the armed freedom struggle for India's liberation as Supreme Commander of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj). Coined the immortal national greeting 'Jai Hind' and mobilized thousands across Asia, delivering decisive blows to British imperial confidence.

15.name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
15.significance: Chief architect of the Constitution of India, world-renowned jurist, and economist who led the historic movement for Dalit rights and the eradication of social untouchability. Enshrined equal rights, civil liberties, and progressive labor laws into the foundation of the world's largest democracy.

16.name: Albert Einstein
16.significance: Fundamentally transformed our understanding of space, time, gravity, and energy. Formulated the Special and General Theories of Relativity and the mass-energy equivalence equation E=mc^2. His Nobel Prize-winning work on the photoelectric effect was pivotal to the emergence of quantum physics.

17.name: Abraham Lincoln
17.significance: Preserved the United States through its greatest existential crisis, the American Civil War, while defeating the Confederacy. Issued the Emancipation Proclamation and secured the Thirteenth Amendment, legally abolishing slavery in the United States and elevating democracy to its highest moral ground.
